summary: Registered the one identified direction from this run's evidence that has no experiment yet, so a continuation has a sourced question with a concrete discriminator instead of a sentence in a limitation. The new investigation @q_stale_snapshot_propagation asks whether the configuration a node writes into its snapshot metadata - which this run shows can be an older or empty membership although the node's log establishes a newer one - can reach another node through InstallSnapshot, since a leader ships its newest snapshot when a follower's next index falls below its compacted log start and installSnapshot installs that snapshot's committed configuration and index (raft.go:1960-1961) before the follower applies the entries sent above the snapshot index. It records two rival readings both consistent with the source: a transient one, where the configuration entries the leader re-sends above the snapshot index correct the joiner's state, and a persistent one, where those entries are absent because the leader's log was trimmed or because the leader's own tracked configuration is the stale one, so the joiner's decision state would stay on the older membership even though its own log and stores were never damaged. The discriminator is a compacted-log leader whose snapshot carries a pre-removal configuration plus a fresh voter joiner, comparing the joiner's tracked configuration after the install and after the subsequent entries against the leader's configuration entries and the committed configuration. The run's two defect accounts and their receipts are unchanged; this batch creates only that investigation.
